title: Cooking oil and water do not dissolve into one solution
summary: Cooking oil and water do not mix into a real solution, because the pull between water molecules is a poor match for oil.
body: OpenStax Chemistry says cooking oils and water will not mix to any appreciable extent to yield a solution. Water is held together largely by hydrogen bonding. The oil molecules are nonpolar hydrocarbons held by dispersion forces, and they do not hydrogen-bond. Making one solution would mean pulling those strong water links apart for very little payoff when the unlike molecules meet. Ethanol, by contrast, does mix with water in any proportion, because both can hydrogen-bond. The page is about whether a solution forms. It is not a washing instruction.
